A.depoimento: I have ordered the assault on the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora to expand our territory. I sent spearmen to Santarem and knights to Evora, exploiting the counter triangle to ensure victory. I also built an archer in the capital to bolster its defenses.
A.plano: Capture Santarem and Evora to expand and secure resources. Build an archer in Lisboa to increase garrison. Keep archers in capital for defense. Next turn, assess the map and prepare to move towards Coimbra and Faro.

B.depoimento: I have ordered a two-pronged assault on the neutral settlements of Tarragona and Girona to expand my domain and secure vital resources. Simultaneously, the blacksmiths in Barcelona have been tasked with forging two additional spearmen to bolster our defenses. The march of conquest begins now!
B.plano: My primary goal is to quickly expand to 18 villages to secure the win condition. I will start by capturing the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona, which are adjacent to my capital Barcelona. This will increase my resource income and provide a buffer zone. From there, I will push west and south into the unexplored territories, seeking to connect with and eventually capture enemy villages, while maintaining a strong defense at Barcelona. I will prioritize building spearmen for their cost-effectiveness and counter capabilities against knights.

A.depoimento: I order my spearmen to take Coimbra and my archers to march on Faro, two neutral villages that will expand my domain. In the capital, I build more archers to grow my forces. With these captures, I will hold five villages and open roads to new lands.
A.plano: Conquer Coimbra with spearmen from Santarem (counter bonus vs knight) and Faro with archers from Lisboa (counter bonus vs spearmen). Build 2 archers in capital for future use. Keep 3 knights in Evora as reserve. After captures, assess newly visible villages (Porto, Salamanca, Sevilha) and plan next expansion toward 18 villages.

A.depoimento: Our archers assault Badajoz, while knights ride to join the vanguard. In our homeland, we forge spearmen to secure our borders and fuel our expansion.
A.plano: We attacked Badajoz with 3 archers from Faro; they should conquer it next turn. We sent 2 knights from Evora to reinforce Badajoz (arrive in 2 turns). We built 2 spearmen in Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora to increase our troop pool. Next turn, consolidate Badajoz, start building in Coimbra and Faro, and prepare to explore towards Toledo. Keep an eye on enemy movements.

B.depoimento: We strike at dawn! Tarragona's garrison marches on Castellon, while Girona's forces assault Huesca. We will swallow these neutral villages whole and use them as stepping stones to flood the peninsula with our might. Barcelona forges the steel of our conquest—two knights rise from its forges to ride into battle!
B.plano: Expand east and west from my current borders. Take Castellon and Huesca this turn to secure footholds. Next turn, use the new garrisons and reinforced troops to push towards Zaragoza and the unexplored territories. Build knights in Barcelona for heavy hitting power, and spearmen in Tarragona/Girona to replenish losses and form spear-heavy armies to counter enemy knights. Aim to connect my villages and slowly push the front line towards the enemy capital, capturing 18 villages to win.

A.depoimento: We launched an attack on Porto with archers from Lisboa to secure the northern route. We also reinforced Coimbra with spearmen and sent an archer to Badajoz to prepare for the southern push towards Sevilha, while building new troops across our villages.
A.plano: Conquer Porto with 2 archers from Lisboa. Reinforce Coimbra with spearmen from Santarem and Lisboa to prepare for Salamanca. Send 1 archer from Faro to Badajoz to prepare for Sevilha. Build spearmen and archers to grow our army. Watch for enemy movements.

B.depoimento: This turn, our armies conquer Zaragoza and Valencia, expanding our territory. We send reinforcements to the front lines to prepare for the next phase of our campaign. The kingdom grows stronger.
B.plano: Take Zaragoza and Valencia this turn to secure footholds. Next turn, reinforce the new garrisons and build up Tarragona and Huesca as staging points. Push towards Teruel and Pamplona, then west to Madrid and beyond. Build spearmen and archers to counter expected enemy knights and spearmen. Aim to connect all villages and reach 18 to win.

A.depoimento: I have launched a double offensive: Porto and Sevilha. My archers are already marching to Porto, and I am sending 7 spearman from Coimbra to finish the job. From Badajoz, I am sending all my archers and knights to seize Sevilha. I am building spearman and archers in every village to maintain my army's strength.
A.plano: Conquer Porto and Sevilha. The archers from Lisboa and spearman from Coimbra should take Porto. The Badajoz force should take Sevilha. Build troops to replace losses and prepare for Salamanca and Toledo. Watch for enemy movements.

A.depoimento: This turn, I ordered the assault on Cordoba, sending my elite archers and knights from Sevilha to crush the neutral garrison. Meanwhile, I marched spearman from Porto and Santarem to Coimbra, forming a mighty spearhead for the capture of Salamanca. Across my realm, I built new troops: spearmen in Lisboa, Santarem, Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro, a knight in Evora, and an archer in Faro, replenishing my ranks and preparing for further expansion.
A.plano: Attack Cordoba with Sevilha's archers and knights. Send spearman from Porto and Santarem to Coimbra to gather for Salamanca next turn. Build spearman in most villages, a knight in Evora, and an archer+spearman in Faro to rebuild. Do not attack Salamanca until Coimbra has at least 8 spearman. Prepare for Vigo by building archers in Porto next turn. Watch for enemy movements.

B.depoimento: Our armies assault Zaragoza! Tarragona's forces attack the neutral village, while reinforcements are sent to prepare for the next pushes. Builders work to expand our armies.
B.plano: Capture Zaragoza this turn to open the west. Next turn, attack Madrid from Zaragoza and Teruel from Castellon. Reinforce Huesca for Pamplona. Continue building troops to reach 18 villages and hold them for two turns.

A.depoimento: This turn we launched a decisive attack on Salamanca with a mighty spear force from Coimbra. We reinforced our key villages of Coimbra and Badajoz, and built up our archer corps for the next phase. We are preparing to strike Toledo and Vigo soon.
A.plano: Attack Salamanca with Coimbra's 14 spear. Reinforce Coimbra with Santarem's 2 spear and Badajoz with Faro's 3 spear. Build archers in Porto and Sevilha for Vigo and Murcia. Next turn, attack Toledo with Badajoz's gathered force (9 spear). Build archer in Cordoba to prepare for Murcia. Do not attack Vigo yet; wait for archers to gather. Watch for enemy movements near Coimbra and Badajoz.

B.depoimento: I order the simultaneous assault on Teruel and Madrid. My spearman lead the charge, countered by their knights, and I expect to secure both villages this turn.
B.plano: Attack Teruel and Madrid this turn to expand my territory. Focus on building archers in Castellon and Valencia for the next targets: Murcia and Pamplona, which are guarded by spearmen. Use the newly captured villages to push into the unexplored north and west.

A.depoimento: Our armies attack Madrid and Toledo this turn. We send spearmen from Salamanca and Badajoz to conquer these key villages. Meanwhile, we start moving archers to the fronts of Vigo and Murcia, and our villages produce troops for the next waves.
A.plano: Capture Madrid (11 spear from Salamanca) and Toledo (9 spear from Badajoz). Move archers: Faro->Sevilha, Lisboa->Santarem->Coimbra, Sevilha->Cordoba, to prepare Vigo/Murcia attacks. Build max spearman everywhere except Salamanca.

B.depoimento: This turn, I am reinforcing the attack on Teruel with troops from Valencia and Zaragoza, while sending Huesca's army to take Pamplona. I am building a mix of spears, archers, and a knight to prepare for the next targets: Murcia, Burgos, and Toledo.
B.plano: Send Valencia and Zaragoza troops to reinforce Teruel. Send Huesca army to attack Pamplona. Build spears in Tarragona, Girona, Zaragoza; archers in Castellon, Huesca, Valencia; and a knight in Barcelona. Next turn, attack Murcia from Valencia/Castellon and Burgos from Pamplona/Madrid.

A.depoimento: My armies moved! Madrid's spear seized Zaragoza. I reinforced my key villages: Coimbra to Porto, Sevilha to Cordoba, Badajoz to Toledo, and Faro to Sevilha. I built knights and spearmen across my realm. Next turn, Vigo and Murcia will be mine!
A.plano: This turn: capture Zaragoza with Madrid's 6 spear. Reinforce Porto from Coimbra (3 spear, 1 archer), Cordoba from Sevilha (2 spear, 1 archer), Toledo from Badajoz (4 spear), and Sevilha from Faro (4 spear). Build a mix of spear and knights. Next turn: attack Vigo from Porto and Murcia from Cordoba; send Salamanca's troops to Madrid; prepare attacks on Burgos and Teruel.

B.depoimento: We launched a strong counter-attack from Teruel, sending our elite forces to conquer the enemy village of Toledo. At the same time, we are reinforcing our borders at Zaragoza and Huesca, while preparing the assault on the neutral village of Murcia by moving our archers from Castellona to Valencia. Our army is growing, and we will soon hold the key to the entire peninsula!
B.plano: Attack Toledo from Teruel to conquer an enemy village and secure the southern front. Send Castellon's archers to Valencia to prepare the attack on Murcia. Reinforce Zaragoza with Tarragona's troops and Huesca with Girona's troops to hold the borders. Build knights in Barcelona, Tarragona, Zaragoza; archers in Girona, Castellon, Huesca, Valencia. Next, conquer Murcia and Pamplona, then push towards Burgos and Madrid.

A.depoimento: This turn, I ordered my armies to strike at the neutral villages of Vigo and Murcia, and the enemy village of Teruel, to expand my territory and secure resources. I also sent reinforcements to my border villages of Madrid, Toledo, and Porto to ensure our defenses remain strong as we push eastward. Additionally, I ordered the construction of knights across my realm to bolster our offensive capabilities for the battles to come.
A.plano: Capture Vigo, Murcia, and Teruel this turn. Reinforce Madrid from Salamanca, Toledo from Badajoz, Porto from Coimbra, and Sevilha from Faro. Build knights in all major villages to grow our army. Next turn, consolidate our new territories and prepare to attack Burgos and Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: My armies attack Murcia and Burgos, conquering them and expanding my realm. I reinforce Zaragoza to secure the northern border. My troops are building across the land to prepare for the next pushes.
B.plano: Conquer Murcia and Burgos to expand my territory and gain resources. Reinforce Zaragoza with troops from Tarragona and Huesca to hold the border against Madrid. Build spearmen in all villages to grow my army. Next, push towards Cordoba from Murcia and towards Madrid from Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: I am launching a major offensive against Madrid with the bulk of my army from Zaragoza. Reinforcements are moving up from Tarragona and Huesca to secure the capital, while Castellon sends troops to Valencia to strengthen the southern border. All villages are building spearmen and archers to swell my ranks.
B.plano: Conquer Madrid to break the enemy line. Send reinforcements to Zaragoza and Pamplona to secure the border. Reinforce Valencia from Castellon to protect the south. Build troops in all villages to grow my army. Next, push towards Salamanca and Toledo from Madrid, and secure Burgos from Pamplona.

A.depoimento: We are mobilizing our forces, sending troops to the borders and building up our army. Our goal is to capture Burgos and then push into enemy territory. We hope to overwhelm the enemy with our numbers.
A.plano: We are building archers in most villages to create a large army that counters enemy spearmen. We are sending these reinforcements to Salamanca and Toledo to prepare for attacks on Madrid and Teruel. In Porto, we are building knights to capture the neutral village Burgos, which will expand our territory and provide a northern base. We must wait until next turn to launch the Burgos attack with the newly built knights. We are leaving some troops in our interior villages for defense.

B.depoimento: Ordered the assault on Toledo and Salamanca from Madrid, utilizing the counter triangle to overcome Toledo's defenses. Reinforcements are flowing from Zaragoza, Valencia, and Huesca to secure the newly conquered territories and prepare for the push into enemy heartlands.
B.plano: This turn, we launch a decisive strike from Madrid to break the enemy front. We attack Toledo with archers and a knight to exploit the counter triangle, and send a large force to the empty Salamanca to secure a foothold. Simultaneously, we flow reinforcements from Zaragoza, Valencia, and Huesca to our front-line villages to consolidate our gains and prepare for the next push towards the enemy capital. We focus our building on knights and archers to maintain our tactical advantage.

A.depoimento: Our army is growing stronger every turn as we build archers across the realm. We are coordinating our movements to concentrate overwhelming force at Madrid, Teruel, and Burgos. The enemy will not be able to withstand our synchronized assault. The path to victory is clear!
A.plano: We are building archers in all possible villages to maximize our reinforcement capacity. We are sending the available archers from Coimbra, Badajoz, Faro, and Cordoba to Salamanca and Toledo to combine with the incoming reinforcements for the attacks on Madrid and Teruel. In the north, we are sending Vigo's knights to capture the neutral Burgos, while Porto's knights march to Vigo to secure the route. We must hold our fire in Salamanca and Toledo until the combined stacks are ready to overwhelm the enemy defenses.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launched a decisive double strike to expand our empire. From Madrid, our knights and archers swept across the neutral Burgos, overcoming its archer garrison to claim our eleventh village. In the east, Valencia's knights and spearmen crushed the enemy's archers at Murcia, capturing a twelfth village from King A. To ensure our front line remains unbreakable, we flowed reinforcements from Zaragoza into Madrid, while our villages worked tirelessly building knights and archers to sustain our campaign. The net is closing in on the enemy!
B.plano: We launch a double offensive this turn to expand our territory towards the 75% threshold. We attack the neutral village [14] Burgos from [12] Madrid with 3 knights and 2 archers, exploiting the knight-archer counter triangle to overcome its 4 archers and defense of 10. Simultaneously, we attack the enemy village [15] Murcia from [16] Valencia with 3 knights and 2 spearmen, also using the counter triangle to defeat its 4 archers and defense of 10. We reinforce [12] Madrid from [17] Zaragoza with 2 knights and 1 archer to maintain its strength as our primary front-line hub. We build knights and

A.depoimento: Today we launch a three-pronged attack: Salamanca strikes Madrid, Toledo takes Teruel, and Vigo conquers Burgos. Our archers pour out of every village to swell the ranks. The enemy will be overwhelmed by our numbers!
A.plano: Attacking Madrid, Teruel, and Burgos with all available troops. Sending archers from interior villages to reinforce the front lines. Building archers in all villages to maintain momentum. Next turn, check the results of the attacks and prepare to push into Zaragoza, Valencia, and Pamplona. Do not attack Murcia yet, wait for reinforcements from Sevilha.

B.depoimento: We have launched a swift offensive on the southern front, sending 2 knights from [15] Murcia to crush the weak garrison at [11] Cordoba. In preparation for future assaults, we have heavily reinforced our northern border at [14] Burgos and our eastern stronghold [13] Teruel, while maintaining the strength of [12] Madrid. Our war machine continues to produce knights across the realm, ready to expand our territory.
B.plano: This turn we strike at the weak southern enemy village [11] Cordoba with 2 knights from [15] Murcia, securing a vital foothold and opening the path to the unexplored [9] Sevilha. Simultaneously, we mass our forces for a northern push: we send the entire garrison of [19] Pamplona and 3 knights from [12] Madrid to reinforce [14] Burgos, preparing to assault [10] Vigo next turn. We also bolster our eastern defenses by sending 3 knights from [17] Zaragoza and 2 from [18] Castellon to [13] Teruel, while keeping [12] Madrid strong with 3 knights from [17]. Our war machine focuses on knight productio

A.depoimento: This turn, my armies launched a coordinated strike on the enemy's eastern and northern borders. From Cordoba, my archers took Murcia. From Teruel, my forces split to capture Valencia and Castellon. Meanwhile, the powerful garrison from Madrid marched on Zaragoza, securing its fall. With these four victories, I have reached my target of 18 villages and now control 75% of the map!
A.plano: Conquered Murcia, Valencia, Castellon, and Zaragoza to reach 18 villages. Next turn, focus on defending the newly conquered villages and reinforcing Madrid, Teruel, and Cordoba with the newly built spearmen. Prepare to push towards Pamplona and the enemy capital if possible, but prioritize holding 18 villages for the second consecutive turn.

B.depoimento: Our scouts reveal that [10] Vigo is almost undefended, with an effective defense of only 5. We are striking with a knightly charge from Burgos to claim it. In the south, we are massing forces at Murcia to crush Cordoba next turn. The enemy's strongholds at Teruel and Madrid remain our long-term targets, but we will bleed them by taking their weaker peripheral villages first.
B.plano: This turn we focus on exploiting the enemy's weak peripheral defenses. We launch a decisive knightly charge from [14] Burgos to capture the lightly defended [10] Vigo, opening the northern front. Simultaneously, we reinforce [15] Murcia with a knight from [16] Valencia and build a knight there to prepare for the assault on [11] Cordoba next turn. We also consolidate our interior troops towards the front lines, moving forces from Barcelona, Girona, Huesca, and Pamplona to strengthen our border garrisons at Tarragona, Castellon, Zaragoza, and Burgos, ensuring we have the manpower to push deeper

B.depoimento: This turn, we strike at the enemy's weak borders while preparing for the inevitable counter-offensive. Vigo's knights conquer Porto, and Burgos's spearmen and archers take Madrid, securing our northern flank. As the enemy masses for an assault on Castellon, we rush knights from Tarragona to reinforce its defenses, while Barcelona, Girona, and Pamplona send troops to bolster Tarragona and Huesca. We build spearmen and knights across our territory to replenish our ranks and prepare for the push into Cordoba, aiming to turn the tide of this war.
B.plano: We are launching a two-pronged offensive on the weakly defended enemy periphery while shoring up our interior defenses. From the north, Vigo's knights will take Porto, and Burgos will capture Madrid, securing our northern flank and turning Burgos into an interior village. In the east, we reinforce Castellon against the incoming enemy assault by sending knights from Tarragona, while Barcelona, Girona, and Pamplona send troops to Tarragona and Huesca to maintain a strong front against Zaragoza. In the south, Murcia builds spearmen to prepare for the assault on Cordoba next turn. We build across

B.depoimento: My armies march on Teruel and Cordoba! While the enemy is distracted, I reinforce my northern borders, sending troops to Pamplona and Madrid. The war for Spain begins in earnest, and I will not yield an inch of my father's land!
B.plano: This turn, I launch a multi-pronged offensive against the weak enemy villages of Teruel and Cordoba, while reinforcing my northern and central fronts. Troops from Castellon will take Teruel, and Murcia will take Cordoba, expanding my territory. Simultaneously, I send reinforcements from Huesca to Pamplona and Burgos to Madrid to shore up my defenses against the stronger enemy holdings like Zaragoza and Toledo. Next turn, I will build on these gains by attacking Coimbra with newly trained archers from Porto, aiming to open a western front and move towards the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: King A orders the simultaneous assault on Cordoba, Teruel, Pamplona, and Murcia! Our armies strike at the enemy's weakest points, and our builders work overtime to replenish our ranks. The crown will triumph!
A.plano: Launch a coordinated offensive on four fronts: Toledo takes Cordoba, Zaragoza splits forces to take Teruel and Pamplona, Valencia takes Murcia. Rebuild troops immediately to maintain momentum and defense.

A.depoimento: My armies strike on four fronts! Toledo and Zaragoza coordinate to take Teruel, Valencia sweeps Castellon, Zaragoza sends a force to Pamplona, and Salamanca assaults Porto. My builders work overtime to refill my ranks.
A.plano: Launch a coordinated offensive on four fronts: Toledo takes Teruel, Valencia takes Castellon, Zaragoza splits forces to take Pamplona, and Salamanca assaults Porto. Rebuild troops immediately to maintain momentum and defense. Focus on weak enemy villages to reach 18 villages.

B.depoimento: This turn, we fortified our eastern border by sending our elite knights from Castellon to defend Teruel against the imminent enemy assault. We initiated a massive troop redistribution along the Zaragoza front, swapping spearmen and knights between Huesca, Pamplona, and Girona to form a powerful knight-led army in Huesca. In the center, we moved spearmen from Madrid to Burgos and brought archers and knights to Madrid to prepare for an attack on Zaragoza. We also commissioned the construction of 22 knights across our entire territory to ensure our armies have the superior counter-tactics against
B.plano: Our campaign focuses on defending Teruel from the incoming enemy army by reinforcing it with knights from Castellon. Simultaneously, we are consolidating our forces on the Zaragoza front by swapping troops between Huesca and Pamplona, and Girona to Huesca, to create a knight-majority army in Huesca. We also shift spearman from Madrid to Burgos and bring knights to Madrid to prepare a knight-majority attack from Madrid. We build knights across all our villages to maximize our offensive power against the enemy's archer-heavy garrisons. Next turn, we will launch coordinated attacks on Zaragoza fr

A.depoimento: Our armies strike at Vigo and Madrid while the force at Pamplona secures our third target. We rebuild our ranks across the realm to sustain the offensive and hold our new territories.
A.plano: Attack Vigo from Porto and Madrid from Salamanca to secure two key enemy villages. Our army marching to Pamplona should conquer it, bringing us to 18 villages. Rebuild troops across all villages to maintain momentum and prepare for the next turn's defense.

B.depoimento: This turn, we mobilized our entire front line to strike at the enemy's weakest points. Our knights led the charge from Huesca to Zaragoza and from Teruel to Valencia, while our spearmen and archers advanced from Burgos to Vigo and Tarragona to Castellon. We built new knights and spearmen to reinforce our ranks and ensure our home villages remain defended. The simultaneous offensive aims to overwhelm the enemy's defenses and secure four new villages, bringing us closer to our goal of holding 18 villages or eliminating the enemy threat entirely.
B.plano: Our campaign focuses on a multi-front offensive to expand our territory and secure our borders. This turn, we launch simultaneous attacks on four weak enemy villages: Zaragoza, Vigo, Castellon, and Valencia. We will use our strongest knight-heavy armies to exploit the enemy's archer garrisons with the counter triangle bonus. By taking these four villages, we shift our front line forward, link our eastern and western fronts, and increase our village count to 10. We will keep small garrisons in our home villages to defend against any counter-attacks. In the coming turns, we will consolidate our

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered all my villages to build knights and launched a coordinated strike on four enemy villages: Vigo, Castellon, Madrid, and Pamplona. I moved my rear forces to the front lines to consolidate my army. If all goes well, I will conquer four villages in one turn, bringing my total to 12 and severely weakening King A's territory.
B.plano: Launch a massive 4-front offensive this turn to conquer Vigo, Castellon, Madrid, and Pamplona simultaneously. Build knights in all villages to maximize offensive power. Send rear troops (Barcelona, Girona) to border villages (Tarragona, Huesca) to reinforce them and prepare for the next wave. Move troops from Teruel and Tarragona to Zaragoza to build a massive army for the next turn's push towards Toledo and Salamanca. This will bring our total villages to 12, putting us well on our way to the 18 needed for victory.

A.depoimento: We strike on three fronts simultaneously! Toledo sends its knights to Teruel, Murcia its spearmen to Valencia, and Pamplona its knights to Burgos. At the same time, Coimbra reinforces Porto and Salamanca to secure our northern borders, while Cordoba sends archers to Murcia to hold the line. Our villages are busy building knights to swell our ranks for the next phase of the campaign. The enemy will find our borders well defended and our offensive unstoppable!
A.plano: Launch a three-front offensive: Toledo to Teruel, Murcia to Valencia, Pamplona to Burgos. Reinforce Porto and Salamanca from Coimbra to secure the north, and send archers from Cordoba to Murcia to hold the line after our offensive. Build knights in all villages to grow our army for the next turn.

B.depoimento: Our forces conquered Vigo, Castellon, and Madrid last turn, bringing our total to 11. This turn, we strike at the enemy's weak points: Porto, Salamanca, and Pamplona. We are gathering a massive army in Zaragoza for the next phase of our campaign. The enemy's capital is within our sights, but we will take our time to ensure victory.
B.plano: This turn, we attack the weak enemy villages: Porto from Vigo, Salamanca from Madrid, and Pamplona from Zaragoza. We gather a massive army in Zaragoza by sending reinforcements from Tarragona and Barcelona. Castellon's knights reinforce Valencia for the southern push. Build knights everywhere to sustain the offensive. Next turn, with 14 villages, use the Zaragoza horde to attack Toledo, then push towards the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: This turn, we ordered a three-front offensive: Pamplona to Burgos, Teruel to Castellon, and Porto to Vigo. We sent reinforcements from Coimbra, Badajoz, Murcia, Valencia, and Toledo to secure our borders and prepare for the next phase. We built knights in nearly all our villages to strengthen our army. Our goal is to reach 18 villages and hold them for victory.
A.plano: We are attacking Burgos, Castellon, and Vigo this turn to reach 18 villages. We are sending reinforcements from Coimbra to Porto, Badajoz to Toledo, Murcia to Valencia, and Valencia and Toledo to Teruel to secure our borders and prepare for counterattacks. We are building knights in almost all villages to grow our army. We decided not to attack Madrid this turn as it is stronger and we want to focus on easier targets. Next turn, we must check if we have conquered the three targets and send additional reinforcements to hold them.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered a coordinated assault on three fronts, targeting the enemy's weakest settlements: Pamplona, Valencia, and Salamanca. My armies were victorious, but not without cost. I am now sending reinforcements to secure the newly conquered lands and rebuild my forces for the next push towards the enemy's heartland.
B.plano: We launch a multi-pronged attack on the enemy's weak villages: Pamplona, Valencia, and Salamanca. Zaragoza leads the assault on Pamplona, Madrid on Salamanca, and Castellon on Valencia. We send all available troops to these targets. Reinforcements from interior villages (Tarragona, Barcelona, Huesca, Girona, Burgos) are dispatched to the front lines to hold captured territories and prepare for the next wave. We build knights and archers to replenish losses. After securing these villages, we will push towards Toledo and Teruel, then explore the south to find more enemy villages.

A.depoimento: Our armies struck at the weak eastern targets of Tarragona and Huesca while simultaneously reinforcing our embattled border villages of Pamplona and Castellon. The twin offensives aim to secure the 18 villages needed for victory, while our growing knight force prepares for the next phase of the campaign.
A.plano: We are attacking Tarragona and Huesca to reach 18 villages. We are reinforcing Pamplona and Castellon against expected enemy attacks. We are building knights in all possible villages to grow our army. We must hold the new conquests for 2 consecutive turns to win.

B.depoimento: Turn 30: My armies converge on the enemy's weak points. The giant force from Zaragoza strikes Pamplona, while Madrid and Vigo unite to take Burgos. Salamanca's knights leap to Coimbra. I build knights and archers across my realm to replenish my forces. The western front is secured as Vigo becomes interior, and the path to Porto opens.
B.plano: Focus on the weak enemy villages of Burgos and Coimbra this turn, attacking from Madrid/Vigo and Salamanca respectively. Simultaneously, the massive army from Zaragoza should take Pamplona. Reinforce Tarragona and Huesca to prepare for the next pushes towards Castellon and Teruel. After securing Burgos and Coimbra, Vigo becomes an interior village, and we can safely push towards Porto and Badajoz. Build up troops in all villages to maintain the momentum.
